# EnterpriseGlue v0.37.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.36.1`.

## Highlights

- **cloud-authentication:** Enforce the configured company sign-in policy on managed tenant sessions.
- **cloud-authentication:** Support Cloud sign-in with a Microsoft application registered for organizational and personal accounts.
- **cloud-onboarding:** Bind managed Cloud organization requests to a verified account and deliver request notifications through the host email service.
- **cloud-authentication:** Require a verified second factor for configured managed Cloud platform administrators.
- **host-dashboard:** Expose a dashboard slot for first-run project and engine setup actions.
- **documentation:** Let a verified managed Cloud user open documentation through the existing account handoff.
- **oracle-images:** Retain Oracle publication receipts in GHCR and provide verified inputs for manual documentation catch-up.

## User and administrator impact

- After a tenant enables company-only sign-in, users must use an enabled company identity provider to enter that organization.
- A first-time Microsoft sign-in confirms the account email by opening a one-time link.
- Returning users sign in with the same Microsoft account and keep their existing Cloud identity.
- Organization request emails reflect the verified requester and the current request status.
- A platform administrator uses an operator identity provider that attests MFA or an enrolled user-verifying passkey.
- A compatible Cloud plugin can guide new workspace administrators into the existing setup flows.
- Cloud signup describes organization requests and explains that email sign-in works with a one-time link and offers optional passkey setup.
- Verified users can open documentation from their profile when the account gateway is configured.
- Operators can verify Oracle image publication when GitHub Actions artifact storage is unavailable and prepare a private documentation draft when automatic handoff is pending.

## API and integration compatibility

- Adds a tenant sign-in policy reset for an authorized platform administrator recovery session.
- Adds browser-bound Microsoft email verification request, link and completion routes.
- Adds an opt-in requester claim to the existing platform Cloud identity exchange.
- Adds a private, release-bound endpoint for organization notifications.
- Adds an authenticated exchange for a short recovery session from a recent verified platform sign-in.
- Adds a dashboard frontend slot with permission-aware workspace setup actions.
- A gateway-authenticated documentation session can retrieve the current verified email at GET /api/auth/documentation/subscriber.

## Configuration

- Enable a company identity provider and verify the administrator's linked identity before disabling other sign-in methods.
- Use the Microsoft common v2.0 issuer for a managed Cloud provider registered for work, school and personal accounts.
- Configure the exact Web callback and a working email sender before enabling the provider.
- Set EG_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION_REVIEW_EMAIL and configure the default host email provider.
- Use the exact HTTPS application origin and match the release controller credentials to the serving release.
- Set EG_CLOUD_PLATFORM_ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED after verifying the independent platform sign-in and recovery methods.
- Use the same dedicated documentation gateway credential on both services.

## Database migrations

- Uses the existing Cloud email proof store with a separate proof purpose.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Tenant entry and session refresh recheck that company-only sessions still use an enabled company provider.
- The recovery endpoint checks platform tenancy management permission and the administrator recovery session and writes an audit event.
- The common discovery issuer is resolved from the signed directory claim and the signing key's issuer is checked.
- A mutable email claim cannot create a Microsoft-backed session or attach a subject to an existing account.
- The host rechecks the authenticated account and its current session before attesting requester identity.
- The notification endpoint accepts fixed message types and checks the verified recipient.
- The host checks verified MFA when issuing, refreshing and accepting platform administrator sessions.
- Recovery rechecks current platform administrator membership and serializes session creation against source session revocation.
- Recovery token renewal and tenant switching preserve the original session deadline.
- Each setup action uses the current permission decision and the existing application workflow.
- The existing browser proof, single-use grant, exact source session, account eligibility and gateway credential remain required.
- The publisher requires independent verification of the receipt signed by the protected workflow before reporting successful publication.

## Known limitations

- Staging company identity provider and operator recovery acceptance require an actual configured provider.
- The Microsoft registration and email delivery must be configured on the deployed environment.
- Requires a compatible Cloud control plane and a configured email sender.
- The deployment must verify that the operator identity provider supplies recognized MFA evidence.
- The host requires a compatible frontend plugin to render the setup panel.
- The subscriber gateway must support the handoff and have a matching configured account origin.
- Previously published images can be verified through their existing signatures, build provenance and SBOM attestations.

## Rollback

- Restore the previous compatible host version using the deployment's normal release rollback procedure.
- Restore the previous compatible host and frontend release together.
- Restore a compatible control plane and host together.
- Restore the prior compatible host and frontend configuration.
- Restore the previous compatible host and plugin composition.
- Disable the gateway handoff before restoring an earlier host version.
- Use the retained signature and build provenance for an existing Oracle image digest.

## Validation evidence

- Restricted PostgreSQL tests verified profile linking, one user identity, tenant enforcement, refresh and authorized policy recovery.
- Focused OpenID Connect, route contract, frontend and restricted PostgreSQL checks passed.
- Focused notification, authorization and restricted PostgreSQL requester-attestation checks passed.
- Native PostgreSQL tests cover verified sign-in, refresh, short recovery, tenant switching, CSRF, company policy recovery, and denial for an ordinary member.
- Focused frontend workflow tests and type checks.
- Focused route, frontend and strict authorization contract checks.
- The release canary checks the exact Cosign commands and verifies the signed receipt against a scratch image digest.
